To solve this inequality, we take the intersection of the two solution sets to each of the two inequalities and . To solve the first one, we have

Then, Rearranging and factoring: We know that , so we can set to obtain . For the next solutions, we can use the quadratic formula on the equation : \begin{align*} a = 35 \pm \sqrt{1225 - (1000 + 70\{a\})} = 35 \pm \sqrt{225-70\{a\}} \end{align*} Since \(a = 35 \pm \sqrt{225 - 70\{a\}}\) must produce real values of \(a\) that satisfy \(\lfloor a \rfloor = a - \{a\}\), the expression inside the square root must correspond to a value of \(a\) whose integer part stays consistent. Therefore, we only consider values of \(\{a\}\) that make \(a\) land near an integer, which happens when \(\sqrt{225 - 70\{a\}}\) is close to an integer.
